newsitem.title: ITALY: Agnelli junior, heir to Italy's Fiat, has tumour.
newsitem.headline: Agnelli junior, heir to Italy's Fiat, has tumour.

text.p: Giovanni Alberto Agnelli, the nephew and appointed heir of former Fiat chairman Gianni Agnelli, said on Sunday he had a rare, but curable stomach tumour.

"I have to stay for a few months in the United States because of a health problem that I have discovered only a few days ago," he said in an interview with La Stampa newspaper, which is owned by the powerful Agnelli family.
"I don't think this should be a secret, they have diagnosed that I have a tumour," he said
The 32-year-old Agnelli, who is chief execuitve of Piaggio scooter-maker, got married last November to British-American architect Avery Howe.
Agnelli said in the interview that Howe was pregnant and would stay with him during the treatment in New York.

"My (type of) illness has already been studied and cured. It won't be a brief cure. This they have told me from the start, but I should be completely back to health by the end of the summer," he said.
He told the newspaper he started to suffer stomach pains a few months ago but thought it was a simple infection. He was diagnosed as having a tumour after Easter.
Agnelli has been head of Piaggio since 1993 and also sits on the board of Fiat -- Italy's largest private company.
He was designated heir apparent to the Fiat empire in 1995 and was widely expected to take the reins of power in June 1998, when current Fiat chairman Cesare Romiti is due to retire.

But Agnelli said in an interview last year that it was wrong to suggest he would automatically take over, adding that he would do so only if the Fiat board considered him the most suitable person for the job.
